title: "4: jSSc ASCT monocytes longitudinal analysis"
output: html_notebook
---

In this notebook, we run our longitudinal monocyte pseudobulk offset analysis. Adapted from Lee and Han (2024).

We begin by loading in useful packages and custom functions.

First, clear the environment and set the path where the project folder is saved.

```{r}
# Clear all objects from environment
rm(list = ls(all.names = TRUE))
# Free up memory
gc()
# Increase max vector memory
mem.maxVSize(200000)

project_path <- "/Users/juliaelrod/Desktop/cmu/research/scleroderma/jSSc_ASCT_monocytes_manuscript/code_for_manuscript/"

results_dir <- paste0(project_path, "data/DEG_pathway_CSVs/")
```

Now load in useful packages and custom functions.

```{r}
# Load packages
packages <- c("Seurat", "dplyr", "tidyr", "SeuratDisk", "harmony", "readr",
              "ggplot2", "stringr", "SoupX", "dsb", "data.table", "Matrix",
              "scDblFinder", "scater", "ggrepel","tidyverse", "RColorBrewer", "pheatmap",
              "clusterProfiler", "enrichplot", "msigdbr", "patchwork", "grid", "gridExtra", "ggtext", "ggh4x", "gtable")
invisible(lapply(packages, require, character.only = TRUE))

# Source functions
function_files <- list.files(paste0(project_path, "functions"), pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)
invisible(lapply(function_files, source))
```

We run the model on all the patient monocytes. 

```{r}
# Read in monocytes
monocytes_r <- LoadH5Seurat(paste0(project_path, "data/h5seurat/monocytes_r_2.h5seurat"))

# Subset out patient monocytes
SSc_monocytes_r <- subset(monocytes_r, health == "SSc")

# Design
design_formula <- ~ subject + poly(timepoint)

# Fit offset pseudobulk model
pbo_monocytes_r <- pb_offset(
  seurat_obj = SSc_monocytes_r,
  sample_id_variable = "sample_id",
  design_formula = design_formula)

# Test for significant effect of time since ASCT
results <- test_de(pbo_monocytes_r$fit, `poly(timepoint)`) %>% 
  arrange(pval)

# Save all results
write_csv(results, paste0(results_dir, "all_DE_results.csv"))
```

Now we conduct pathway enrichment analysis based off of this tutorial:  https://biostatsquid.com/pathway-enrichment-analysis-tutorial-clusterprofiler/

Setup for GSEA is below:

```{r}
# Get hallmark, GO biological process, and GO cellular component pathways
hallmark_sets <- msigdbr(species = "human",
                         collection = "H")
bp_sets <- msigdbr(species = "human",
                   collection = "C5",
                   subcollection = "GO:BP")
cc_sets <- msigdbr(species = "human",
                   collection = "C5",
                   subcollection = "GO:CC")
# Store all sets together
all_sets <- rbind(hallmark_sets, bp_sets, cc_sets)

# TERM2GENE
term2gene <- all_sets %>%
  select(gs_name, gene_symbol)

# TERM2NAME (readable descriptions)
term2name <- all_sets %>%
  distinct(gs_name, gs_description)

# Background genes
DefaultAssay(SSc_monocytes_r) <- "RNA"
background_genes <- rownames(SSc_monocytes_r)
```

Let's run pathway analysis for each direction separately.
 
```{r}
# (1) PBMC

# Add direction (whether expression goes up or down over time) to results data frame
results_sig <- results %>% filter(pval < 0.05) %>% mutate(direction = case_when(
  lfc > 0 ~ 'UP',
  lfc < 0 ~ 'DOWN',
))

# Split the dataframe into a list of sub-dataframes: upregulated, downregulated genes
results_list <- split(results_sig, results_sig$direction)

# Run enricher R on each set of genes (up set and down set)
gsea <- lapply(names(results_list),
              function(x) enricher(
                  gene = results_list[[x]]$name,
                  TERM2GENE = term2gene,
                  TERM2NAME = term2name,
                  universe = background_genes,
                  pvalueCutoff = 1,
                  qvalueCutoff = 1,
                  minGSSize = 5,
                  maxGSSize = 500
              )) %>% setNames(names(results_list))

# View results
# DOWN
gsea$DOWN@result %>% head(20)
# UP
gsea$UP@result %>% head(20)
```

Note from a reviewer: Do these genes behave similarly in classical vs non-classical monocytes, or are there subsets that are restricted to one of the two large monocyte subpopulations seen?

We investigate below: 

```{r}
# Subset out CD14 patient monocytes
cd14_SSc_monocytes_r <- subset(SSc_monocytes_r, cell_type == "CD14+")
cd16_SSc_monocytes_r <- subset(SSc_monocytes_r, cell_type == "CD16+")

# Design (same as before)
design_formula <- ~ subject + poly(timepoint)

# Fit offset pseudobulk models
# CD14
pbo_CD14_monocytes_r <- pb_offset(
  seurat_obj = cd14_SSc_monocytes_r,
  sample_id_variable = "sample_id",
  design_formula = design_formula)
# CD16
pbo_CD16_monocytes_r <- pb_offset(
  seurat_obj = cd16_SSc_monocytes_r,
  sample_id_variable = "sample_id",
  design_formula = design_formula)

# Test for significant effect of time since ASCT
results_CD14 <- test_de(pbo_CD14_monocytes_r$fit, `poly(timepoint)`) %>% 
  arrange(pval)
results_CD16 <- test_de(pbo_CD16_monocytes_r$fit, `poly(timepoint)`) %>% 
  arrange(pval)

# Add direction (whether expression goes up or down over time) to results data frame
results_CD14_sig <- results_CD14 %>% filter(pval < 0.05) %>% mutate(direction = case_when(
  lfc > 0 ~ 'UP',
  lfc < 0 ~ 'DOWN',
))
# Add direction (whether expression goes up or down over time) to results data frame
results_CD16_sig <- results_CD16 %>% filter(pval < 0.05) %>% mutate(direction = case_when(
  lfc > 0 ~ 'UP',
  lfc < 0 ~ 'DOWN',
))



# For both sets of genes, check whether it is in results_sig and whether the direction matches

# Track # of matches between broad monocyte results and CD14+ results
CD14_match_total <- 0
# Track names of matches between broad monocyte results and CD14+ results
CD14_match_list <- c()
# Track # of matches between broad monocyte results and CD16+ results
CD16_match_total <- 0
# Track names of matches between broad monocyte results and CD16+ results
CD16_match_list <- c()

# Loop over all significant genes in broad monocyte model
for (sig_gene in results_sig$name) {
  # Check if significant in CD14+ model & if the direction is the same
  if (sig_gene %in% results_CD14_sig$name && results_CD14_sig[which(results_CD14_sig$name == sig_gene), "direction"] == results_sig[which(results_sig$name == sig_gene), "direction"]) {
    # Add to match count
    CD14_match_total <- CD14_match_total + 1
    # Add gene name to match list
    CD14_match_list <- c(CD14_match_list, sig_gene)
  }
  # Check if significant in CD16+ model & if the direction is the same
  if (sig_gene %in% results_CD16_sig$name && results_CD16_sig[which(results_CD16_sig$name == sig_gene), "direction"] == results_sig[which(results_sig$name == sig_gene), "direction"]) {
    # Add to match count
    CD16_match_total <- CD16_match_total + 1
    # Add gene name to match list
    CD16_match_list <- c(CD16_match_list, sig_gene)
  }
}

# Get intersection between significant CD14+ and CD16+ genes
intersect_list <- intersect(CD14_match_list, CD16_match_list)
# Get # of genes in the intersection
intersect_count <- intersect_list %>% length()
# Number of unique CD14+ genes
CD14_unique_count <- CD14_match_total - intersect_count
# Number of unique CD16+ genes
CD16_unique_count <- CD16_match_total - intersect_count

# Get full results for these genes from broad monocyte model
intersect_sig <- results_sig[results_sig$name %in% intersect_list, ]

# Split the dataframe into a list of sub-dataframes: upregulated, downregulated genes
intersect_results_list <- split(intersect_sig, intersect_sig$direction)

# Check directions of unique CD14+ and CD16+ genes
results_sig[results_sig$name %in% setdiff(CD14_match_list, intersect_list), ] %>% pull(direction) %>% table()
results_sig[results_sig$name %in% setdiff(CD16_match_list, intersect_list), ] %>% pull(direction) %>% table()


# GSEA
# Run enricher R on each set of genes (up set and down set)
gsea_intersect <- lapply(names(intersect_results_list),
              function(x) enricher(
                  gene = intersect_results_list[[x]]$name,
                  TERM2GENE = term2gene,
                  TERM2NAME = term2name,
                  universe = background_genes,
                  pvalueCutoff = 1,
                  qvalueCutoff = 1,
                  minGSSize = 5,
                  maxGSSize = 500
              )) %>% setNames(names(intersect_results_list))

# View results
# DOWN
gsea_intersect$DOWN@result %>% head()
# UP
gsea_intersect$UP@result %>% head()
```

We will add a column to results_sig that indicates whether the gene is significant in both classical/non-classical monocytes, one, the other, or neither

```{r}
results_sig$subtype <- ""
results_sig[results_sig$name %in% intersect_list, "subtype"] <- "Both"
results_sig[results_sig$name %in% setdiff(CD14_match_list, intersect_list), "subtype"] <- "CD14+"
results_sig[results_sig$name %in% setdiff(CD16_match_list, intersect_list), "subtype"] <- "CD16+"
```

Out of the top statistically significant pathways with increasing and decreasing activity, we select the most biologically relevant pathways and display them in bar charts below.

First, pathways with decreased activity over time since ASCT:

```{r}
# Data frame mapping pathway IDs to formal pathway names
down_pathways_to_show <- data.frame(full_name = c("HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB",
                           "HALLMARK_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE",
                           "GOBP_EPITHELIAL_CELL_DIFFERENTIATION",
                           "HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING",
                           "HALLMARK_IL2_STAT5_SIGNALING",
                           "HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS"
                           ), plot_name = c("TNF-α signaling via NF-κB (Hallmark)",
                                            "Inflammatory response (Hallmark)",
                                            "Epithelial cell differentiation (GOBP)",
                                            "TGF-β signaling (Hallmark)",
                                            "IL2-STAT-5 signaling (Hallmark)",
                                            "Apoptosis (Hallmark)"))

# Create data frame including results for these pathways
gsea_down_df <- down_pathways_to_show %>%
  inner_join(
    gsea$DOWN@result %>% select(ID, p.adjust, pvalue, FoldEnrichment),
    by = c("full_name" = "ID")
  )

# Bar chart
gsea_down_plot <- ggplot(data = gsea_down_df, 
                         aes(x = -log10(p.adjust),
                             y = reorder(plot_name, -p.adjust),
                             fill = reorder(plot_name, -p.adjust))) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues") +
  theme_bw() +
  ylab("Gene set") +
  xlab(expression("-log"[10]*"adjusted p-value")) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 15),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 15),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, width = 25))
# Save as PNG
ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/gsea_down_plot.png"), gsea_down_plot, width = 6.5, height = 5)
```

Now, we make a tile plot showing the top 5 most statistically significant longitudinal DEGs for our top decreasing pathways.

```{r}
# Get all gene sets
gene_sets_down <- gsea$DOWN@geneSets
# Select top pathways
favorite_down_pathways <- down_pathways_to_show$full_name
fav_gene_sets_down <- gene_sets_down[favorite_down_pathways]

# Make a named vector of p-values for quick lookup
pval_lookup_down <- results %>% filter(lfc < 0) %>% pull(pval)
names(pval_lookup_down) <- results %>% filter(lfc < 0) %>% pull(name)

# Order each pathway's genes by p-value
fav_gene_sets_down_ordered <- lapply(fav_gene_sets_down, function(genes) {
  # Keep only genes that exist in results
  genes_in_results <- intersect(genes, names(pval_lookup_down))
  
  # Order by p-value
  genes_in_results[order(pval_lookup_down[genes_in_results])]
})

# Get top 5 genes for each pathway and take intersection
topgenes_down <- lapply(fav_gene_sets_down_ordered, function(x){head(x, 5)}) %>% unlist() %>% setNames(NULL) %>% unique()

# Matrix indicating which genes are in which pathway
pathway_by_gene_mat_down <- sapply(topgenes_down, function(gene) {
  sapply(fav_gene_sets_down_ordered, function(x) gene %in% x)
})

# Turn into data frame
heat_df_down <- pathway_by_gene_mat_down %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("pathway") %>%
  pivot_longer(-pathway, names_to = "gene", values_to = "present")

# Add gene to DF
heat_df_down$gene <- factor(heat_df_down$gene, levels = topgenes_down)

# Left join with gsea_down_df (formal pathway names for plotting)
heat_df_down <-
heat_df_down %>%
    left_join(
        gsea_down_df %>% select(full_name, plot_name),
        by = c("pathway" = "full_name")
    )

# We use same palette as prior pathway plot
down_gb <- ggplot_build(gsea_down_plot)
down_fill_mapping <- 
data.frame(
  full_name = down_gb$plot$data$full_name,
  fill = unique(down_gb$data[[1]]$fill)
)


# Create new variable with fill color
heat_df_down <- heat_df_down %>%
  left_join(down_fill_mapping, by = c("pathway" = "full_name")) %>%
  mutate(fill_color = ifelse(present, fill, "white"))


# Genes to bold (in 3 + pathways)
pathway_counts <- levels(heat_df_down$gene) %>% lapply(function(GENE){heat_df_down %>% filter(gene == GENE) %>% pull(present) %>% sum()}) %>% setNames(levels(heat_df_down$gene)) %>% unlist()
genes_to_bold <- pathway_counts[pathway_counts >= 3] %>% names()

# Named vector: gene -> styled label
gene_labels <- heat_df_down %>%
    distinct(gene) %>%
    mutate(label = ifelse(gene %in% genes_to_bold,
                          paste0("<b>", gene, "</b>"),
                          as.character(gene))) %>%
    tibble::deframe()

# Set levels of pathway
heat_df_down$plot_name <- factor(
  heat_df_down$plot_name,
  levels = down_gb$layout$panel_params[[1]]$y$breaks
)

# Plot it
gsea_plot_with_genes_down <- 
  ggplot(heat_df_down, aes(x = gene, y = plot_name, fill = fill_color)) +
    geom_tile(color = "black") +
    # Thick outline around full columns of bolded genes (adjacent columns share one box)
    geom_rect(
      data = data.frame(x = sort(match(genes_to_bold, levels(heat_df_down$gene)))) %>%
        group_by(run = x - row_number()) %>% # consecutive positions share the same run id
        summarise(xmin = min(x) - 0.5, xmax = max(x) + 0.5),
      aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0.5, ymax = nlevels(heat_df_down$plot_name) + 0.5),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 2.5
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_identity() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none",
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 13),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 15, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 15, face = "bold"),
    ) +
    ylab("Gene Set") +
    xlab("Gene") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, width = 25)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = gene_labels) +
  theme(axis.text.x.bottom = element_markdown(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11))

ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/gsea_down_plot_with_genes.png"), gsea_plot_with_genes_down, width = 7, height = 5, bg = "white")
```

```{r}
# Set levels of pathway
heat_df_up$plot_name <- factor(
  heat_df_up$plot_name,
  levels = up_gb$layout$panel_params[[1]]$y$breaks
)

# Named vector: gene -> styled label
gene_labels <- heat_df_up %>%
    distinct(gene) %>%
    mutate(label = ifelse(gene %in% genes_to_bold,
                          paste0("<b>", gene, "</b>"),
                          as.character(gene))) %>%
    tibble::deframe()

# Plot it
gsea_plot_with_genes_up <- 
  ggplot(heat_df_up, aes(x = gene, y = plot_name, fill = fill_color)) +
    geom_tile(color = "black") +
    # Thick outline around full columns of bolded genes (adjacent columns share one box)
    geom_rect(
      data = data.frame(x = sort(match(genes_to_bold, levels(heat_df_up$gene)))) %>%
        group_by(run = x - row_number()) %>% # consecutive positions share the same run id
        summarise(xmin = min(x) - 0.5, xmax = max(x) + 0.5),
      aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0.5, ymax = nlevels(heat_df_up$plot_name) + 0.5),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 2.5
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_identity() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none",
      #text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 13),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 15, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 15, face = "bold")
    ) +
    ylab("Gene Set") +
    xlab("Gene") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, width = 25)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = gene_labels) +
  theme(axis.text.x.bottom = element_markdown(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11))

ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/gsea_up_plot_with_genes.png"), gsea_plot_with_genes_up, width = 7, height = 5, bg = "white")
```

Now we will produce longitudinal plots for the genes shown in the tile plots.

```{r}
# Plot with custom function

ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/gene_plots_down_combined.png"),
```

Now, we make a reduced version of the downward DEGs to be included in one of the main figures.

```{r}
# Select group of decreasing DEGs to show
# 1) CDKN1A. 279 hits on PubTator with SSc. Upregulated in SSc skin.
# 2) FOSL1. Of interest to Torok lab. AP-1 Transcription Factor. Related to proteins in JUN family. 67 hits on PubTator with SSc. Association with SSc somewhat unclear.
# 3) SMAD3. 1118 hits on PubTator with SSc. Upregulated in SSc.
# 4) PPARG. 847 hits on PubTator with SSc. Circulating levels elevated in SSc.
# 5) CTNNB1. 1128 hits on PubTator with SSc. Upregulated
# 6) EMP1. One of the top statistically significant genes. 12 hits on PubTator with SSc.
six_down_degs <- c("CDKN1A",
                   "FOSL1",
                   "SMAD3",
                   "PPARG",
                   "CTNNB1",
                   "EMP1")

# Clean individual plots

})

# Caption as blank plot.

# Stack plots + caption, collect legend, add title via plot_annotation
```

Now, we'll make some volcano plots showing DEGs that go up and down over time since ASCT. We highlight the same pathway-involved genes we used above, as well as the top 10 genes in each direction.

```{r}
# Top 10 genes that go up
top10_up <- results %>% arrange(pval) %>% filter(lfc > 0.5) %>% pull(name) %>% head(10)
# Key upward pathway genes
pathway_genes_up <- heat_df_up$gene %>% levels()
# Take union
up_highlight <- union(top10_up, pathway_genes_up)
# We don't want to show genes without a name
up_highlight <- up_highlight[!grepl("ENSG", up_highlight)]

# Top 10 genes that go down
top10_down <- results %>% arrange(pval) %>% filter(lfc < -0.5) %>% pull(name) %>% head(10)
# Key downward pathway genes
pathway_genes_down <- heat_df_down$gene %>% levels()
# Take union
down_highlight <- union(top10_down, pathway_genes_down)

# Create new data frame for plotting (mutation of results from pb offset)
volc_results <- results %>%
  mutate(`Trend following ASCT` = case_when(
    lfc > 0.5 & pval < 0.05 ~ "Up",
    lfc < -0.5 & pval < 0.05 ~ "Down",
    TRUE ~ "Not significant"
  )) %>%
  mutate(delabel = case_when(
    name %in% c(up_highlight, down_highlight) ~ name,
    TRUE ~ NA
  ))

# Put significance levels in proper order
volc_results$`Trend following ASCT` <- factor(volc_results$`Trend following ASCT`, levels = c("Up", "Down", "Not significant"))

# Save as RDS for supporting data values file
Fig3ADat <- volc_results %>% 
  mutate(highlight = case_when(
    is.na(delabel) ~ FALSE,
    .default = TRUE
  )) %>%
  select(name,
         pval,
         adj_pval,
         lfc,
         highlight)
saveRDS(Fig3ADat, paste0(project_path, "data/supporting_data_values/3A.RDS"))

# Volcano plot
jSSc_longitudinal_volcano <- ggplot(data = volc_results, aes(x = lfc, y = -log10(pval), col = `Trend following ASCT`, label = delabel)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.5, 0.5), col = "gray", linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), col = "gray", linetype = 'dashed') + 
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(0,20,0,0), color = 'black'),
        axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", margin = margin(20,0,0,0), color = 'black'),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black", size = 25),
        legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.2, 0.2),
legend.background = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.4)),
legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red3", "#00AFBB", "grey")) +
  labs(x = expression("log"[2]*"FC"), y = expression("-log"[10]*"p-value")) + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-10, 10, 2)) +
  geom_label_repel(#max.overlaps = Inf,
                  # size = rel(3),
                  box.padding = 0.3,
                  force = 4,
                  show.legend = F,
                  na.rm = T,
                  size = 6.5)

# Save as PNG
ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/jSSc_longitudinal_volcano.png"), jSSc_longitudinal_volcano, width = 14, height = 10)
```

We also make a volcano plot comparing jSSc and Healthy.

```{r}
# Make sure default assay is set to RNA
DefaultAssay(monocytes_r) <- "RNA"

# Run pb offset for baseline and healthy, where we are testing group membership (two-way comparison) rather than time coefficient.
SSc_v_h_PB <- pb_offset(subset(monocytes_r, group %in% c("baseline", "healthy")), "sample_id", ~health)
# Test DE
SSc_v_h_PB_results <- SSc_v_h_PB$fit %>% test_de("healthSSc") %>% arrange(pval)

# We save the top 50 upregulated DEGs and top 50 downregulated DEGs as CSV
top50_up_results <- SSc_v_h_PB_results %>% filter(lfc > 0.5) %>% head(50)
top50_down_results <- SSc_v_h_PB_results %>% filter(lfc < 0.5) %>% head(50)
# Write CSV
write_csv(top50_up_results, paste0(project_path, "data/DEG_pathway_CSVs/SSc_v_healthy/top50_SSc_v_healthy_monocytes_UP.csv"))
write_csv(top50_down_results, paste0(project_path, "data/DEG_pathway_CSVs/SSc_v_healthy/top50_SSc_v_healthy_monocytes_DOWN.csv"))

# Genes to highlight (biologically interesting)
ssc_v_h_up_highlight <- c("CARD19", "PIK3R1", "IL15RA", "GAB1", "MEF2A", "MAP3K3", "GRB2", "CXXC5", "GPR35", "LBR", "CDKN2D", "PICALM", "CELF2", "NINJ1")
ssc_v_h_down_highlight <- c("FARSA", "CARD9", "MS4A7", "PLD4", "UBE2S", "HLA-DRB1", "DUSP2", "GADD45B", "F13A1", "BAIAP2", "TIAM1", "FLCN", "ANG", "PARP1", "RNASEH2B", "EIF2S1", "ABCC5")

# Create new data frame for plotting (mutation of results from pb offset)
SSc_v_h_PB_volc_results <- SSc_v_h_PB_results %>%
  mutate(`SSc baseline vs. Healthy` = case_when(
    lfc > 0.5 & pval < 0.05 ~ "Up",
    lfc < -0.5 & pval < 0.05 ~ "Down",
    TRUE ~ "Not significant"
  )) %>%
  mutate(delabel = case_when(
    name %in% c(ssc_v_h_up_highlight, ssc_v_h_down_highlight) ~ name,
    TRUE ~ NA
  ))

# Put significance levels in proper order
SSc_v_h_PB_volc_results$`SSc baseline vs. Healthy` <- factor(SSc_v_h_PB_volc_results$`SSc baseline vs. Healthy`, levels = c("Up", "Down", "Not significant"))

# Save as RDS for supporting data values file
Fig2FDat <- SSc_v_h_PB_volc_results %>% 
  mutate(highlight = case_when(
    is.na(delabel) ~ FALSE,
    .default = TRUE
  )) %>%
  select(name,
         pval,
         adj_pval,
         lfc,
         highlight)
saveRDS(Fig2FDat, paste0(project_path, "data/supporting_data_values/2F.RDS"))

# Volcano plot
SSc_v_h_volcano <- ggplot(data = SSc_v_h_PB_volc_results, aes(x = lfc, y = -log10(pval), col = `SSc baseline vs. Healthy`, label = delabel)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.5, 0.5), col = "gray", linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), col = "gray", linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(0,20,0,0), size = rel(1.1), color = 'black'),
        axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", margin = margin(20,0,0,0), size = rel(1.1), color = 'black'),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = rel(1.1)),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c( "red3", "#00AFBB", "grey")) +
  labs(x = expression("log"[2]*"FC"), y = expression("-log"[10]*"p-value")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-10, 10, 2)) +
  geom_label_repel(max.overlaps = Inf,
                  size = 6.5,
                  box.padding = 0.3,
                  force = 4,
                  show.legend = F,
                  na.rm = T) +
  labs(col = "SSc baseline \nvs. Healthy")
# Save as PNG
ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/SSc_v_healthy_pb_volcano.png"), SSc_v_h_volcano, width = 14, height = 6)
```

We assign a biological annotation to each cluster

```{r}
monocytes_r@meta.data <- monocytes_r@meta.data %>%
  mutate(
    bio_annotation = case_when(
      # Marker genes = highlighted genes in data/annotation_deg_CSVs/monocyte_annotation/<cell type>/cluster_<n>.xlsx
      seurat_clusters == 0 ~ "0. CD14+ CXCL8+ TNFAIP6+ IL1B+ TNFAIP3+ PADI4+",
      seurat_clusters == 1 ~ "1. CD14+ S100A12+ CSF3R+ NCF1+ ALOX5AP+ TREM1+",
      seurat_clusters == 2 ~ "2. CD14+ S100A8+ S100A9+ RNASE2+ RETN+",
      seurat_clusters == 3 ~ "3. CD14+ CCL3+ F13A1+ EREG+ FCER1A+",
      seurat_clusters == 4 ~ "4. CD16+ CDKN1C+ SIGLEC10+ C1QA+",
      seurat_clusters == 5 ~ "5. CD16+ HLA-DPB1+ HLA-DRB1+ CD74+ HLA-DQA1+",
      seurat_clusters == 6 ~ "6. CD14+ CD99+ LGALS2+ SERPINE1+ IGFBP7+",
      seurat_clusters == 7 ~ "7. CD14+ CCL2+ PPARG+ CCL7+ TNFRSF12A+ CD109+",
      seurat_clusters == 8 ~ "8. CD14+ IFI44L+ SIGLEC1+ RSAD2+ IRF7+ TNFSF13B+",
      TRUE ~ paste0(seurat_clusters, ". ", cell_type)
    )
  )

# Cluster to highlight: drawn on top with larger points, circled, and labelled off to the side
target_cluster <- 7
callout_pos    <- c(x = -5.0, y = 3.7)   # centre of the target's label box, in UMAP coordinates (read off the axes)

# Annotations in cluster order (sets legend order and colours)
annotation_levels <- monocytes_r@meta.data %>%
    distinct(seurat_clusters, bio_annotation) %>%
    arrange(seurat_clusters) %>%
    pull(bio_annotation)
annotation_cols <- setNames(scales::hue_pal()(length(annotation_levels)), annotation_levels)

# One row per cell; target cluster sorted last so it is drawn on top
umap_df <- Embeddings(monocytes_r, "wnn.umap") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    mutate(annotation = factor(monocytes_r$bio_annotation, levels = annotation_levels),
           is_target  = monocytes_r$seurat_clusters == target_cluster) %>%
    arrange(is_target)

# One label per cluster, placed at the median of its cells
label_df <- umap_df %>%
    group_by(annotation, is_target) %>%
    summarise(x = median(wnnUMAP_1), y = median(wnnUMAP_2), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(label = str_wrap(annotation, width = 15))
target <- filter(label_df, is_target)

# Label boxes: white for most clusters, a lighter shade of the cluster colour for the target.
# Blank rows for a sample of target cells make ggrepel keep the other labels off them.
set.seed(42)
repel_df <- bind_rows(
    label_df %>% mutate(fill = ifelse(is_target, colorRampPalette(c(annotation_cols[[as.character(target$annotation)]], "white"))(100)[66], "white")),
    umap_df %>% filter(is_target) %>% slice_sample(n = 300) %>%
        transmute(x = wnnUMAP_1, y = wnnUMAP_2, label = "", fill = "white", is_target = FALSE)
)

monocyte_bio_umap <-
    ggplot(umap_df, aes(wnnUMAP_1, wnnUMAP_2, colour = annotation)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = is_target)) +
    # Circle the target cluster
    annotate("point", x = target$x, y = target$y, size = 52, shape = 21, colour = "black", stroke = 3) +
    # All labels in one layer so none overlap; the target's label is nudged out with a pointer back to the cluster
    geom_label_repel(data = repel_df, aes(x, y, label = label, fill = fill), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                     nudge_x = ifelse(repel_df$is_target, callout_pos["x"] - target$x, 0),
                     nudge_y = ifelse(repel_df$is_target, callout_pos["y"] - target$y, 0),
                     max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 42, box.padding = 0.5, max.time = 5, max.iter = 1e5,
                     fontface = "bold", size = 6.5, linewidth = 1, segment.size = 2) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = annotation_cols, name = NULL) +
    scale_size_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 2), guide = "none") +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4))) +
    cowplot::theme_cowplot() +
    theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 22),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 22))

# monocyte_bio_umap

# Save as PNG
ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/bio_annotation_umap.png"),
       monocyte_bio_umap, width = 21, height = 13, bg = "white")

# Save updated Seurat object with bio. annotations
# SaveH5Seurat(monocytes_r, paste0(project_path, "data/h5seurat/monocytes_r_3.h5seurat"))
```

```{r}
# Markers to show
# Marker genes per cluster (names = cluster numbers)
bio_marker_groups <- list(
    "0" = c("CXCL8", "TNFAIP6", "IL1B", "TNFAIP3", "PADI4"),
    "1" = c("S100A12", "CSF3R", "NCF1", "ALOX5AP", "TREM1"),
    "2" = c("S100A8", "S100A9", "RNASE2", "RETN"),
    "3" = c("CCL3", "F13A1", "EREG", "FCER1A"),
    "4" = c("CDKN1C", "SIGLEC10", "C1QA"),
    "5" = c("HLA-DPB1", "HLA-DRB1", "CD74", "HLA-DQA1"),
    "6" = c("CD99", "LGALS2", "SERPINE1", "IGFBP7"),
    "7" = c("CCL2", "PPARG", "CCL7", "TNFRSF12A", "CD109"),
    "8" = c("IFI44L", "SIGLEC1", "RSAD2", "IRF7", "TNFSF13B")
)
bio_markers <- unlist(bio_marker_groups, use.names = FALSE)

monocytes_r$bio_annotation_wrapped_2 <- str_wrap(monocytes_r$bio_annotation, width = 20)

# Only CD14+ and CD16+ clusters (drop B-like, T-like, NK-like)
cd14_cd16_monocytes <- subset(monocytes_r, cell_type %in% c("CD14+", "CD16+"))
kept_clusters <- levels(droplevels(cd14_cd16_monocytes$seurat_clusters))

# One box per cluster: x spans its markers (in bio_markers order), y is its row
marker_boxes <- tibble(cluster = names(bio_marker_groups), n = lengths(bio_marker_groups)) %>%
    mutate(xmax = cumsum(n) + 0.5,
           xmin = xmax - n,
           y    = rev(seq_along(kept_clusters))[match(cluster, kept_clusters)])

dp_bio_markers <- DotPlot(cd14_cd16_monocytes, bio_markers, group.by = "bio_annotation_wrapped_2", cols = c("lightgrey", "darkred"), dot.scale = 10) +
    scale_y_manual(
        breaks = lapply(kept_clusters, function(x){
            cd14_cd16_monocytes@meta.data %>% filter(seurat_clusters == x) %>% pull(bio_annotation_wrapped_2) %>% unique()
        }) %>% unlist(),
        values = rev(seq_along(kept_clusters))   # cluster 0 at the top
    ) +
    # Box each cluster's own markers in that cluster's row
    geom_rect(data = marker_boxes, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.5, ymax = y + 0.5),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  theme(
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
) +
  labs(y = "Monocyte sub-cluster",
       x = "RNA marker")

# Save as PNG
ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/bio_annotation_rna_markers.png"),
       dp_bio_markers, width = 15, height = 9, bg = "white")
```

We use FindMarkers to determine which genes are upregulated in cluster 7 compared to other clusters. Then, we identify genes which are upregulated in cluster 7 and also involved in one of our gene sets of interest (decreasing pathways, which makes sense since cluster 7 disappears over time).

```{r}
# Set Idents to clusters
Idents(monocytes_r) <- "seurat_clusters"

# Find DEGs between clus 7 and other clusters
clus7_markers <- FindMarkers(monocytes_r, ident.1 = 7, assay = "RNA")

# Get signficiant markers
sig_clus_7_markers <- clus7_markers %>% filter(p_val_adj < 0.05 & avg_log2FC > 2) %>% rownames()

# Now, we see which markers appear in our pathways of interest.
cluster_7_markers_per_pathway <- lapply(fav_gene_sets_down, function(gs){gs[gs %in% sig_clus_7_markers]})

# Subset out cluster 7 markers in our pathways
clus7_markers_in_pathway <- clus7_markers[rownames(clus7_markers) %in% unique(unlist(cluster_7_markers_per_pathway)), ]

# We will label with top pathway
clus7_markers_in_pathway$pathway <- NA

# Create gene column
clus7_markers_in_pathway$gene <- rownames(clus7_markers_in_pathway)

# Add pathway (each gene is assigned to the most significant pathway it appears in)
for (pathway in names(cluster_7_markers_per_pathway)) {
  for (gene in clus7_markers_in_pathway$gene) {
    if (clus7_markers_in_pathway[gene, ]$pathway %>% is.na) {
      if (gene %in% cluster_7_markers_per_pathway[[pathway]]) {
        clus7_markers_in_pathway[gene, ]$pathway <- pathway
      }
    }
  }
}

# Add pathway names for plotting
clus7_markers_in_pathway <-
clus7_markers_in_pathway %>%
    left_join(
        down_pathways_to_show %>% select(full_name, plot_name),
        by = c("pathway" = "full_name")
    )

# Group by pathway
clus7_markers_in_pathway <- clus7_markers_in_pathway %>%
  mutate(plot_name = factor(plot_name, levels = down_gb$layout$panel_params[[1]]$y$breaks)) %>%
  arrange(plot_name)

# We use the dotplot function to get scaled averages for our heatmap
dp <- DotPlot(monocytes_r, clus7_markers_in_pathway$gene, group.by = "seurat_clusters")
# Extract data
dp_data <- dp$data
# Store levels of gene variable
lvls <- levels(dp_data$features.plot)
# Join
dp_data <- dp_data %>%
  left_join(
    clus7_markers_in_pathway %>%
      select(gene, plot_name),
    by = c("features.plot" = "gene")
  ) %>%
  rename(pathway = plot_name) %>%
  mutate(features.plot = factor(features.plot, levels = lvls))

# Build alternating fill vector matching your pathway factor levels
strip_fills <- rep(c("grey90", "white"),
                   length.out = length(levels(forcats::fct_rev(dp_data$pathway))))

# Heatmap
clus7_heatmap <-
    ggplot(dp_data, aes(y = features.plot, x = id, fill = avg.exp.scaled)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdYlBu") +
    ggh4x::facet_grid2(                                                         # CHANGED
        forcats::fct_rev(pathway) ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
        switch   = "y",
        labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 15),                                  # ADDED
        strip    = strip_themed(                                                 # ADDED
            background_y = elem_list_rect(fill = strip_fills, color = NA)       # ADDED
        )                                                                        # ADDED
    ) +
    labs(fill = str_wrap("Scaled average expression", 10),
         x = "Monocyte sub-cluster",
         y = "") +
    theme(
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.title = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold"),
        legend.title = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold"),
        legend.text = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold"),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold",
                                         margin = margin(0, 2, 0, 2)),          # CHANGED
        strip.background = element_rect(color = NA),                                      # CHANGED
        strip.switch.pad.grid = unit(0, "pt"),                                  # ADDED
        panel.border = element_blank(),                                         # ADDED
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.3, "lines"),
        legend.position = "bottom"
    )

# Build the gtable
g <- ggplotGrob(clus7_heatmap)

# Find left-axis cells (these hold the gene name labels)
axis_idx <- grep("^axis-l", g$layout$name)

# Inject a matching background rect into each axis cell
# axis-l grobs run top-to-bottom, matching strip_fills order
for (i in seq_along(axis_idx)) {
    bg_rect <- rectGrob(gp = gpar(fill = strip_fills[i], col = NA))
    g$grobs[[axis_idx[i]]] <- grobTree(bg_rect, g$grobs[[axis_idx[i]]])
}

# Draw or save
grid.newpage(); grid.draw(g)

# Save as PNG
ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/clus7_heatmap.png"), g, width = 6, height = 11)
```


Now, we want to compare patients to HC *within cluster 7*.

We do 2 two-way comparisons: SSc baseline vs. healthy, and SSc six months vs. healthy

```{r}
# Subset out cluster 7
clus7 <- subset(monocytes_r, seurat_clusters == 7)

# Set idents
Idents(clus7) <- "group"

# Baseline SSc vs. healthy
baseline_v_h_clus7 <- FindAllMarkers(subset(clus7, group %in% c("healthy", "baseline")), only.pos = T) %>%
  select("p_val", "avg_log2FC", "p_val_adj", "group" = "cluster", "gene")
rownames(baseline_v_h_clus7) <- NULL

# Six months SSc vs. healthy
six_v_h_clus7 <- FindAllMarkers(subset(clus7, group %in% c("healthy", "six")), only.pos = T) %>%
  select("p_val", "avg_log2FC", "p_val_adj", "group" = "cluster", "gene")
rownames(six_v_h_clus7) <- NULL

# Save as CSV
write_csv(baseline_v_h_clus7, paste0(results_dir, "baseline_v_h_clus7.csv"))
write_csv(baseline_v_h_clus7, paste0(results_dir, "six_v_h_clus7.csv"))


```

We will run GSEA on genes upregulated in jSSc at baseline (compared to healthy controls) and then separately on genes upregulated in healthy controls (compared to jSSc at baseline).

```{r}
clus7_jSSc_bas_genes <- baseline_v_h_clus7 %>% filter(group == "baseline") %>% pull("gene")
clus7_healthy_genes <- baseline_v_h_clus7 %>% filter(group == "healthy") %>% pull("gene")

# GSEA
gsea_clus7_jSSc_bas <- enricher(
                  gene = clus7_jSSc_bas_genes,
                  TERM2GENE = term2gene,
                  TERM2NAME = term2name,
                  universe = background_genes,
                  pvalueCutoff = 1,
                  qvalueCutoff = 1,
                  minGSSize = 5,
                  maxGSSize = 500)

# View results
gsea_clus7_jSSc_bas@result %>% pull(ID) %>% head(30)

gsea_clus7_healthy <- enricher(
                  gene = clus7_healthy_genes,
                  TERM2GENE = term2gene,
                  TERM2NAME = term2name,
                  universe = background_genes,
                  pvalueCutoff = 1,
                  qvalueCutoff = 1,
                  minGSSize = 5,
                  maxGSSize = 500)

# View results
gsea_clus7_healthy@result %>% pull(ID) %>% head(30)
```



We need a plot showing cluster 7 proportions by group

```{r}
# Get counts in cluster 7 by group
clus7_counts_by_group <- clus7$group %>% table()
# Get counts in all monocytes by group
monocytes_counts_by_group <- monocytes_r$group %>% table()
# Get proportions in cluster 7 by group
clus7_prop_by_group <- clus7_counts_by_group / monocytes_counts_by_group 
# Put into data frame for plotting
clus7_prop_by_group_df <- clus7_prop_by_group %>% as.data.frame() %>% select("Group" = ".", "Proportion" = "Freq") %>%
  mutate(Group = case_when(
    Group == "healthy" ~ "Healthy",
    Group == "baseline" ~ "SSc. baseline",
    Group == "six" ~ "SSc. 6 mo.",
    Group == "twelve" ~ "SSc. 12 mo.",
    Group == "twen4" ~ "SSc. 24 mo."
  ))
clus7_prop_by_group_df$Group <- factor(clus7_prop_by_group_df$Group, levels = clus7_prop_by_group_df$Group)
clus7_prop_by_group_df <- clus7_prop_by_group_df %>% mutate(
  Health = case_when(
    Group == "Healthy" ~ "Healthy",
    TRUE ~ "SSc"
  )
)

# Bar plot
clus7_prop_plot <- ggplot(aes(y = Proportion, x = Group, fill = Health), data = clus7_prop_by_group_df) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Healthy" = "#377EB8",
    "SSc" = "#E41A1C"
  )) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        text = element_text(size = 28),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.title.x = element_blank()) +
  labs(y = str_wrap("Proportion of CD14+ CCL2+ PPARG+ CCL7+ TNFRSF12A+ CD109+ monocytes", width = 25))

# Save as PNG
ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/clus7_prop_plot.png"), clus7_prop_plot, width = 7, height = 7)
```

We want to investigate the amount of overlap between each of the decreasing gene sets to aid our interpretation.

```{r}
# Intersection between each of the 6 gene sets of interest
pathway_intersect_mat <- 
mapply(function(i){mapply(function(j){length(intersect(i, j))}, fav_gene_sets_down_ordered)}, fav_gene_sets_down_ordered)
# Pretty names
rownames(pathway_intersect_mat) <- down_pathways_to_show[down_pathways_to_show$full_name == rownames(pathway_intersect_mat), ]$plot_name
colnames(pathway_intersect_mat) <- down_pathways_to_show[down_pathways_to_show$full_name == colnames(pathway_intersect_mat), ]$plot_name

# Jaccard similarity (intersection/union)
sizes <- diag(pathway_intersect_mat)
jaccard <- pathway_intersect_mat / 
  (outer(sizes, sizes, "+") - pathway_intersect_mat)
# As a heatmap
jaccard_df <- reshape2::melt(jaccard)
jaccard_plot <- 
ggplot(jaccard_df, aes(Var2, Var1, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", value)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "white", high = "blue2") +
  labs(fill = "Jaccard similarity") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"))
ggsave(paste0(project_path, "figures/4_monocyte_longitudinal_analysis/pathway_jaccard.png"), jaccard_plot, width = 10, height = 7)
```
